\textbf{Cookie-banner blockers cannot see Shopify's sandboxed ad pixels, so the pixels send data before, and despite, the visitor's choice.} (Left) On Shopify stores, ad pixels run in sandboxes of Shopify's Web Pixels Manager (hatched box: a web worker or a sandboxed iframe) and send requests to the ad vendor's servers. The cookie banner of a consent-management platform (CMP) and its script blocker act only in the page, so the blocker's reach stops short of the sandbox (red bar: the blind spot). The only gate before the sandbox is Shopify's consent state (diamond), which is set by Shopify's region default and by what the CMP writes to it. (Right) Three results from 1,358 popular Shopify stores in the Tranco top 200,000, loaded from California. Top: on 205 of 409 stores that showed a banner (50.1\%; Wilson 95\% confidence interval (CI) 45.3--54.9\%), a sandboxed ad pixel sent a request before any choice. Middle: of 19 blocklist entries (an ad vendor that the store's CMP listed as blocked and that had a configured sandboxed Shopify pixel) on the 11 stores whose CMP wrote no `marketing: yes' to Shopify, in 12 the vendor sent an ad request from Shopify's sandbox before any choice (95\% CI clustered by store, Korn--Graubard, 24.0--92.3\%). Bottom: in 146 page loads in which the CMP wrote `marketing: no' to Shopify without a click (the `no'), 525 of 535 third-party pixel sandboxes that declare `marketing' had already started (median 650 ms before the write). Bars: each count as a share of its total; red, consent failed; outlined light grey, the rest.
